leads.title: Russian federal law criminalising distribution of 'propaganda' of non-traditional sexual relationships among minors (2013)
leads.documents: National legal status criminalising LGBTQ propaganda to minors; applies in Sakha Republic as federal law. Documents enforcement basis for censorship and hate-crime increase.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'In 2013, Russia passed a law criminalising the distribution of "propaganda" promoting "non-traditional sexual relationships" among minors'. No URL visible in excerpt.

leads.title: 2022 expansion of propaganda law to all ages and gender transition
leads.documents: Documents expansion to prohibit distribution to anyone regardless of age and to prohibit materials that make minors interested in gender transitions - directly relevant to trans visitor expression risk.
leads.detail: Cited as 'in 2022, the "propaganda" law was expanded to apply to anyone regardless of age group, and to also prohibit the distribution of materials that make minors interested in gender transitions.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Russian July 2023 law banning gender-affirming care and legal gender changes
leads.documents: Documents ban on both gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition outright; core trans legal-status source.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In July 2023, Russia enacted a law banning gender transition which prohibited both gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition outright.' No URL visible.

leads.title: 2024 Russian law banning adoption by citizens/residents of countries that allow gender transitions
leads.documents: Documents state family/adoption machinery around gender transition.
leads.detail: Cited as 'in 2024 passed a law banning the adoption of Russian children by citizens or permanent residents of countries that allow gender transitions.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Supreme Court of Russia ruling November 2023 designating 'international LGBT public movement' as extremist / 22 March 2024 unified list addition
leads.documents: Documents criminalization of LGBT activism/participation/symbols (including rainbow flag) under anti-extremism provisions; enforcement via arrests of club owners and flag displays.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In November 2023, the Supreme Court issued a ruling designating "the international LGBT public movement" as an extremist group' and 'On 22 March 2024, the "international LGBT social movement and its structural units" was formally added to the "unified list of terrorist and extremist organizations and persons".' No URL visible.

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights ruling 2010 fining Russia for pride-parade discrimination (Alexeyev)
leads.documents: Documents rights machinery / enforcement: systemic refusal of pride permits and Court finding of discrimination and support for disruption.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In 2010, the European Court of Human Rights fined Russia for discriminating against the LGBTQ community, after local governments systemically refused to issue permits to pride parades' and 'In 2010, Russia was fined by the European Court of Human Rights, ruling that, as alleged by Alexeyev'. No URL visible.

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - Fedotova and Others v. Russia (2021)
leads.documents: Documents lack of any legal recognition for same-sex relationships as human-rights violation.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In the 2021 case Fedotova and Others v. Russia, the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg ruled that it was a violation of human rights for Russia not to offer any form of legal recognition to same-sex relationships.' No URL visible.

leads.title: United Nations Human Rights Council panel of five expert advisors - report 13 April 2017
leads.documents: Documents UN condemnation of wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya as documented incident/enforcement pattern.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In a report issued on 13 April 2017, a panel of five expert advisors to the United Nations Human Rights Council condemned the wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) report December 2018
leads.documents: Documents confirmation that persecution of LGBTQ persons took place and was ignored by authorities.
leads.detail: Cited as 'A report released in December 2018 by the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) confirmed claims that persecution of LGBTQ persons had taken place and was ignored by authorities.' No URL visible.

leads.title: ILGA-Europe ranking 2024 / 2016 / May 2019
leads.documents: Documents institutional assessment of LGBTQ rights status: Russia ranked worst of 49 European countries in 2024, second least friendly in 2016, 46th of 49 in May 2019.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In 2016, Russia was rated the second least LGBTQ-friendly nation in Europe by ILGA-Europe' and 'In 2024, the status of LGBTQ rights in Russia was ranked the worst out of the 49 countries surveyed' and 'In May 2019, ILGA-Europe placed Russia in 46th place among 49'. No URL visible.
